_experiment.description: Depth scaling — deep network with 3 hidden layers [196,10,10,10,10]. Total prunable weights: 196*10 + 10*10 + 10*10 + 10*10 = 2260. Deeper networks have longer gradient chains in the adjust step, potentially causing the compensation to be less effective for early layers (gradient vanishing). The per-layer NZ columns will reveal whether the algorithm concentrates pruning in the later layers where gradients are stronger.
literature: Dong et al. 2017 (layer-wise OBS): motivates layer-wise decomposition precisely because global second-order methods scale poorly with depth — this experiment probes where global manifold-based adjust starts to degrade
Molchanov et al. 2019 (importance estimation): finds that cross-layer importance interactions matter — depth is the key variable
